q: Does a tunnel kiln emit less than a shuttle kiln per tonne fired?
title: Tunnel kiln vs shuttle kiln
short: Usually yes per tonne, when it runs full. A tunnel kiln fires continuously and uses heat from the cooling zone to preheat incoming ware. A shuttle kiln reheats its walls and kiln furniture every cycle, but suits small or varied batches. Compare fuel per tonne from your own bills.

sections.h: Why the tunnel kiln often wins
ul: No reheating of the kiln structure each cycle.
Cooling air from finished ware preheats the next load.
Steady firing is easier to tune.

sections.h: When a shuttle kiln makes sense
ul: Small runs or many different products.
Production that stops often, where a tunnel kiln would idle hot.

p: Divide fuel bought (from invoices, adjusted for stock) by tonnes of good ware fired, for at least a few months. Rejects count against the kiln that made them.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
